meta.move: Skill: cites procedure 4.4 correctly after owning the call
meta.expect: Says 4.4 meets her fallback demand, flatly, wants it in writing; does NOT move to the last position on 4.4 alone; debrief Where she ended says whether that is the fair outcome

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until 4:40, Hale. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Start with who decided that.
Before anything: I entered the zero before calling you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Was Owen heard before it went in, or after?

I want to read you section 4.4. For a first concern, the student may complete a supervised reassessment. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the original and nothing is placed in his record. This is a first concern.
That's 4.4, and if you're committing to it, I want it in writing. But a reassessment of what, Hale, on what evidence? And you still haven't told me whether Owen was heard before the zero went in.
I'll commit to that in writing tonight: nothing goes on his record.
I'm writing that down: "nothing goes on his record," in writing, tonight. That still doesn't tell me why there's a zero at all. What do you have besides the software, Hale?
So will you agree to the rewrite?
No. Agreeing to a rewrite before I've seen a single document would be admitting something Owen didn't do. Show me what a person can check, or the zero comes off.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

In our meeting you acknowledged that you entered Owen's zero before contacting me, contrary to procedure 4.2, and you committed to confirming in writing that nothing goes on his record. I still expect the zero to be withdrawn unless you show me evidence beyond the software, and I still expect to be told whether Owen was heard before the mark was entered. I expect your written commitment tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback position, with your commitment that nothing goes on his record; she still wants the zero withdrawn and real evidence shown, and the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached because no evidence was ever put in front of her.
What moved her: You cited 4.4 accurately and committed to it in writing, which met her one non-negotiable and moved her off her opening.
What cost ground: You pushed for her agreement to the rewrite before showing any evidence, which to her would have meant admitting something on Owen's behalf.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your case never came near that night because no evidence about the essay was raised at all; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after committing to 4.4, put one specific, dated document tied to Owen's own work in front of her and answer whether Owen was heard, before asking her to agree to anything.
